statement: The first line holds n and k; the second holds the n stream values in arrival order. After each arrival print the kth largest seen so far, or -1 while fewer than k values have arrived - all answers on one line, space-separated. Maintain a min-heap capped at k: push the newcomer, pop the minimum when the size spills past k, and report the root. Each arrival costs log k and the memory stays at k slots however long the stream runs.

example.why: After three arrivals the 3rd largest is 10; 70 evicts it leaving root 11; 50 evicts 11 leaving 20.

hint: The root is the answer the instant the heap reaches size k - no sorting, no scanning.
mistake: Re-sorting everything seen on each arrival; the stream's whole point is paying log k, never n log n.
